encoding_policy.input_encoding: none - slicing is by byte offset, not character. Fields are decoded ISO-8859-1 after slicing (contract C-1.3, C-1.4)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: full: a multi-byte UTF-8 character shifts every later field by its extra byte count and corrupts the record, exactly as the legacy cut does. That corruption is reproduced, not repaired (P-UTF8)
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: none rejected. Bytes > 0x7F raise the ascii_only expectation and are routed to quarantine, and the row still flows through unchanged

malformed_record_policy.details: A '|' byte inside any slice adds fields to the rendered psv line and shifts every downstream consumer by one column (contract C-5.1). Silver stores both the six sliced fields and the rendered psv_line; gold aggregates a re-split of psv_line so the shift is reproduced rather than silently fixed. The no_delimiter_collision expectation attributes it. No field is ever NULL: missing is the empty string (C-3.6), so empty and absent are deliberately indistinguishable, as in the legacy.

empty_input_semantics.details: An empty input file yields an empty parsed result - zero silver rows, no error, matching the legacy 0-byte psv (C-1.6). A blank line inside a file is NOT empty input: it produces a row with all fields empty (C-1.7).

acceptance_checks.description: Silver rows equal the captured .psv line for line: all six fields byte-exact, compared without any whitespace, case or null canonicalization.
Trailing spaces are stripped from cust_id, cust_name and currency only; bill_date, bill_amt and rec_type keep theirs, so record type '1 ' stays '1 ' (C-3.1).
Amount is a strtod-style prefix parse of the 12-byte slice / 100, formatted %.2f: 12AB->0.12, 1e3->10.00, empty->0.00, leading '-' gives a negative amount (C-3.3, C-3.4).
Date is positional slicing with no validity check: 20259999->2025-99-99, 8 spaces->'    -  -  ', empty->'--' (C-3.5).

Lines whose first three bytes are HDR or TRL are deleted, including data records shadowed by that rule; the shadowed row is flagged not_hdr_trl_shadowed in quarantine and is still absent from silver, as in the legacy (C-4.1).
Every expectation is warn-and-route: the quarantine set equals the expected anomaly set exactly, and silver row count is unaffected by quarantining (C-6.1).
trailer_count vs parsed_count is recorded per file in ow_tp.bronze.custbill_trailer_audit and never changes which rows are produced (C-4.3).
A second run produces identical silver content, proven by an actual rerun.

planted_anomalies.description: A data record whose customer id starts with HDR or TRL is deleted by the sed filter. The probe file declared 15 records, 14 were parsed, both numbers were logged and the job exited 0.
A '|' inside a field shifts every downstream field: the date transform is applied to the name remainder and the report reads currency from the raw amount digits.
Dates are never validated, so impossible dates such as 2025-99-99 reach silver and gold.
Amount parsing stops at the first non-numeric byte and accepts a leading sign, so the unsigned copybook field can yield a negative amount and a garbage field silently becomes 0.00.
Short records yield empty trailing fields and long records discard bytes past position 65; neither is reported.
The trailer record count is logged and never enforced (ETL-0187, open since 2011).
The parser redirects all stderr to /dev/null and ends in `|| true`, so a parse failure produces an empty output file and a success exit code.
planted_anomalies.reason: Forcing the underlying cut/paste/awk pipeline to fail requires breaking the legacy script or its host, which the read-only rule forbids. The target fails loudly instead; the divergence is declared rather than tested.
